title: Documentation support (MEAT) for chronic conditions
question: Which chronic condition, if any, is supported for risk adjustment by this note? Ignore the reason for the visit. Choose 'no code' if none is supported.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for hypertension and new onset of knee pain.

HPI: The patient is a 77-year-old female presenting for a routine follow-up of her hypertension and to evaluate persistent right knee pain. She reports that her blood pressure has been stable at home, though she occasionally experiences mild headaches. Regarding her knee, she describes a dull, aching pain in the right patellofemoral joint that has progressively worsened over the last three months. She notes that the pain is most severe when climbing stairs or after prolonged walking. She denies any acute trauma, locking, or instability. She has tried over-the-counter ibuprofen with only minimal relief.

Review of Systems: Negative for chest pain, shortness of breath, or palpitations. Negative for fever, chills, or weight changes. Negative for numbness or tingling in the lower extremities. Positive for localized right knee pain. Negative for urinary symptoms or changes in bowel habits.

Social History: She is a retired school teacher. She lives in a single-story home with her husband. She enjoys gardening and walking in the park. She denies tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History: Her mother had hypertension and a stroke at age 82. Her father had osteoarthritis.

Vitals: BP: 138/84, HR: 72, RR: 16, Temp: 98.6 F, SpO2: 97% on room air.

Recent Labs: HbA1c: 5.8%, eGFR: 74 mL/min, Serum Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL, TSH: 2.1 mIU/L.

Medication List: Lisinopril 20mg daily, Atorvastatin 40mg daily.

Exam: The patient is alert and oriented x3. She appears in no acute distress. Cardiovascular exam shows regular rate and rhythm with no murmurs. Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. Musculoskeletal exam reveals mild tenderness and decreased range of motion in the right knee. No significant joint effusion or erythema is noted.

Assessment: 1. Hypertension: Well-controlled on current medication. 2. Right knee pain: Likely osteoarthritis given the patient's age and clinical presentation.

Plan: Continue Lisinopril 20mg daily. For the right knee, I will start her on a scheduled Naproxen 500mg twice daily for 10 days to manage inflammation. We will also discuss physical therapy for strengthening of the quadriceps. She will return in 4 weeks for a follow-up.

Problem List:
- Hypertension
- Right knee pain
- COPD
explanations: COPD appears only in a problem list and is not addressed in this encounter, so it is not supported for this date of service.

distractors.why: A problem-list entry alone does not show the condition affected care at this visit.
